Explore the repository ↗ Abstract Overview Data collection Results Citation 01 · Motivation Abstract Dexterous Manipulation Benchmark Long-horizon dexterous manipulation remains a fundamental challenge for robot learning, requiring the composition of multiple skills, precise bimanual coordination, generalizable visual understanding, and robust skill transitions. Yet existing manipulation benchmarks largely emphasize isolated skills or support only a limited range of end-effectors, making these capabilities difficult to evaluate systematically. We introduce DexArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate learning and generalization in long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation. DexArena features 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks spanning diverse household and industrial scenarios. Each long-horizon task is composed of explicitly defined stages with physically grounded success conditions, enabling reliable evaluation of both intermediate progress and end-to-end task completion. A unified benchmark interface and verified human-teleoperated demonstrations enable testing different policy learning algorithms, with standardized simulation configurations, scene randomization, trajectory replay, and task-level evaluation. Through extensive baseline experiments, we identify substantial challenges in precise manipulation, generalization to scene variation, and skill composition. DexArena establishes a challenging and reproducible benchmark for developing robot learning methods that move toward generalizable long-horizon dexterous behavior. title: Evaluation — DexArena
text: Evaluation protocol Evaluation Three levels. One physical contract. DexArena separates failures in execution, generalization, and composition while preserving matching task definitions. 01 Stage level Skill execution Run each of the 30 canonical stage environments with its registered robot, horizon, action layout, and physical success predicate. Success rate across fixed seeds Persistent success, not transient contact 29-D single-arm or 58-D bimanual actions 02 Scene level Visual generalization Evaluate every stage on three native scene surfaces using identical object placement and the fixed 256 × 256 policy camera rig. 90 task × scene combinations Shared seeds across algorithms Saved background manifest 03 Sequence level Skill composition Execute two to five dependent stages in their parent long-horizon environment and report complete-sequence success. Stage progress and terminal success Inherited state between stages Single-arm and bimanual tasks Metric contract Report the failure mode, not only the final number. Stage Success Rate Fraction of evaluation episodes whose stage predicate is satisfied for its required hold duration. Cross-scene Average Mean stage success over robocasa_l3_s2, robocasa_l3_s1, and robocasa_l3_s6 with matched seeds. Generalization Gap Difference between the reference collection workspace and native-scene performance. Composition Rate Fraction of complete long-horizon episodes reaching the final task success state. Paper protocol Fifty episodes. Three distinct questions. All six baselines use image observations and robot proprioception, with matched task horizons, randomization and embodiments. Stage and long-horizon success are measured over 50 episodes per task; generalization uses 50 episodes in each of three held-out kitchens without further adaptation. 01 Recorded evaluation seeds The manuscript specifies stage seeds 50000–50049 for ACT and DP. GR00T uses 10001–10050, reused for each generalization scene and the long-horizon protocol. Record the seed manifest alongside each result. 02 Scene-level uncertainty Generalization reports mean ± standard deviation across three scenes. The average row aggregates stage performance within each scene before reporting variation across scenes. 03 Transitions without resets PPO, RLPD, ACT, DP and π0.5 switch between learned stage policies when the stage succeeds. GR00T uses one task model trained on pooled stage data, with a new instruction at each transition. 01 Stage execution 61.4 % Best average success 02 Visual generalization 49.2 % Best average success 03 Full task completion 1.6 % Best average success 01 / 30 stages · training scene Strong individual skills. title: DexArena documentation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / DexArena documentation DexArena documentation Understand the benchmark, follow the research workflows, and cite the DexArena preprint. A benchmark for skills and complete sequences DexArena evaluates long-horizon dexterous manipulation through 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks . The stages expose individual skills; the complete tasks test whether those skills work in sequence, including bimanual coordination and transitions. Task success comes from physical environment predicates, including the task's persistent hold or latch conditions. Start with the task catalog to choose an environment and understand its stage boundaries. The benchmark overview illustrates the task families, while the results compare the six methods evaluated in the manuscript. What is available today Artifact Current status Paper arXiv:2611.02629 ↗ and public PDF ↗ ; a 2026 preprint. Official repository SIPAIR-Elastic/DexArena ↗ . The current public tree contains the README, Apache 2.0 license and repository metadata; the runnable research package is not published there yet. Demonstrations The paper reports 3,000 replay-successful episodes. A public dataset download endpoint has not been supplied. Trained policies The manuscript reports baseline results. Public DexArena checkpoint download endpoints have not been supplied. Evaluation intake The site presents manuscript baseline results. Public community submission intake is not open. The installation and execution examples in this center describe verified interfaces in the research source. They become usable when you already have that source, its assets and compatible dependencies. See Resources & release status before planning a reproduction run. Follow a complete workflow Prepare a research checkout , verify the task registry, and create one canonical environment. Read the configuration contract and run the small wiring check . Inspect demonstrations and replay , then choose a baseline or implement a policy adapter . Freeze the checkpoint and evaluate native-scene transfer and complete sequences with the registered task definitions. Save the reproduction artifacts , calculate task-weighted metrics, and cite the benchmark . Read each score in its own setting Track Evaluation unit Question Stage execution 30 stages; 50 episodes per stage in the training scene Can the policy complete an individual skill from its valid stage reset? Cross-scene generalization 30 stages × 3 native scenes; 50 episodes per pair Does the frozen policy transfer across the named kitchen scenes? Long-horizon composition 10 sequences; 50 episodes per sequence Can the policy finish the complete sequence after a single reset? Stage completion does not imply complete-sequence success. Keep task horizons, success predicates and stage-transition rules fixed. The score protocol explains aggregation and the meaning of scene variation. title: Getting started — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Getting started Getting started Check artifact availability, prepare the research runtime, and create a registered stage environment. Before running an example Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. A usable research setup needs the DexArena task and robot modules, object and workstation assets, a compatible ManiSkill/SAPIEN runtime, and a working renderer. Native kitchen evaluation also needs the corresponding RoboCasa scene assets. Policy training adds its own dataset, model and accelerator requirements. Use the dependency versions and asset layout associated with your research revision. There is no verified public pip install dexarena distribution or one-command asset installer documented here. A generic ManiSkill installation alone does not register the DexArena tasks. Identify the checkout you have git rev-parse HEAD git status --short git ls-files task utils train data_gen Run these read-only checks in the research checkout. Preserve the commit identifier and local changes with your experiment manifest. If the module directories are absent, the Python examples below cannot run from that checkout; the public repository's current README and license are not a simulator package. Keep the runtime environment and robot/task assets together with the source revision used for data collection. Changing task geometry, controller settings or joint definitions can invalidate stored demonstrations. Create one canonical stage The registry supplies the robot and horizon. This example uses the mouse-clicking stage; it does not assume that every task shares its robot or episode length. import gymnasium as gym import task # Registers the research tasks and robot agents. from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings env_id = "SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1" settings = registered_task_settings(env_id) print(settings) env = gym.make( env_id, **settings, num_envs=1, obs_mode="state", sim_backend="physx_cpu", ) try: obs, info = env.reset(seed=10001) print(env.action_space) print(env.observation_space) finally: env.close() registered_task_settings resolves the canonical stage robot, pd_joint_pos controller and registered time limit without constructing a simulator. It accepts the 30 canonical subtasks; use the task registry for complete-sequence environments. A state observation is useful for checking registration. Image policies need their documented camera and preprocessing contract. Choose a formal target task/config/collection_targets.py lists LONG_TASKS , SUBTASKS and the combined 40 collection targets. The broader Gym registry also contains legacy aliases, retired curricula and variants that are not formal benchmark targets. Enumerating every registered environment will overcount the benchmark. utils/dex_tasks.py records task instructions and policy metadata. Use the catalog to select the stage, then verify its exact environment ID against these registries. Read the environment's spaces instead of copying another stage's observation width. Run the first check Continue with Configurations and Quick evaluation . A successful reset verifies the environment wiring; a learned policy still needs the correct model dependencies, checkpoint and adapter. ← Previous DexArena documentation Next → Resources & release status

title: Configurations — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Configurations Configurations Keep task identity, dynamics, joint targets and camera inputs consistent across collection, training and evaluation. Four parts of the environment contract Layer Reference What to preserve Workspace task/config/workspace_rig.py Shared table and arm-root placement; table center x = +0.180 m, platform x = −0.870 m, arm y = ±0.220 m. Simulation task/config/sim_profiles.py Reference profile: 400 Hz physics, 20 Hz control, solver iterations 24/8 and 1 mm contact offset. Task task/config/collection_targets.py and task module Canonical environment ID, reset distribution, robot, episode limit and persistent success conditions. Policy interface utils/dex_tasks.py and camera configuration Instruction, observation fields, joint order, camera profile and image preprocessing. These values describe the reference profile. Save the resolved configuration for your actual task revision. Changing a physical parameter defines a different experiment and may require new demonstrations and replay validation. Query settings and respect action order Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings settings = registered_task_settings("SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1") print(settings["robot_uids"]) print(settings["control_mode"]) print(settings["max_episode_steps"]) Sharpa environment Absolute target layout Single arm · 29 dimensions 7 Panda arm joints → 22 Sharpa hand joints Bimanual · 58 dimensions Left arm 7 → right arm 7 → left hand 22 → right hand 22 The controller receives absolute joint-position targets in radians under pd_joint_pos . Relative model coordinates must be converted before the controller call. Observation widths vary across stages and can change when the task state changes; infer them from the selected environment and dataset metadata. Treat cameras as policy inputs The native-scene evaluation factory enforces the robodex_fixed base/wrist rig at 256 × 256 . It can differ from an environment's ordinary default cameras. Check utils/dex_cameras.py and utils/dex_camera_rigs.py when mapping dataset images to sensors. Record camera names, order, resolution, resize/crop rule, normalization and temporal history. Diagnostic overview renders and operator VR views do not become additional policy observations. A higher-resolution runtime wrist camera is not interchangeable with the benchmark's fixed policy input. Save the resolved configuration For every run, record the source commit and local changes, task ID and fingerprint, robot UID, controller, physics backend, simulation/control rates, horizon, observation schema and camera settings. Add the checkpoint hash, action normalization, language-selection rule and episode seed list. For native scenes, also save env.unwrapped.eval_background_manifest . It captures the background and fixed environment/camera setup. The reproduction guide explains how to pair these settings with per-episode results. ← Previous Resources & release status Next → Embodiments

title: Quick evaluation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Quick evaluation Quick evaluation Check the environment and adapter loop, then evaluate an actual checkpoint with the registered horizon. Start with a small wiring run Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. The GR00T evaluation entry point includes a zero-action stub. With its research runtime dependencies installed, use two short episodes to check environment creation, image observations and the rollout adapter. The stub does not load a learned policy. python -m train.train_groot --evaluate --stub \ --env-id SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1 \ --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cpu \ --camera-size 256 --num-eval-envs 1 \ --num-eval-episodes 2 --num-eval-steps 20 \ --max-episode-steps 500 --seed 10001 \ --instruction-sampling canonical A wiring check has no benchmark interpretation The short rollout intentionally ends before the task horizon. Its success or failure is not a policy score. The stub still requires the research environment and imports used by the entry point. Evaluate a learned checkpoint Replace the example checkpoint path with a compatible, locally available fine-tuned GR00T checkpoint. DexArena checkpoint download URLs have not been published. Keep the adapter and camera contract matched to training. python -m train.train_groot --evaluate \ --env-id SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1 \ --model-path /path/to/checkpoint \ --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cpu \ --camera-size 256 --num-eval-envs 1 \ --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 500 \ --max-episode-steps 500 --seed 10001 \ --instruction-sampling canonical --capture-video The 500-step horizon is registered for this mouse task. Query registered_task_settings for another stage. Here --seed 10001 starts the evaluation episode seed range; preserve the explicit seeds in the result manifest. canonical uses the fixed canonical instruction; the entry point also supports registered instruction sampling. Report which rule you used. Repeat with a frozen policy Add --scene-background robocasa_l3_s2 and repeat with robocasa_l3_s1 and robocasa_l3_s6 . Keep the checkpoint, preprocessing and episode seeds fixed. The native-scene path enforces one CPU environment, the registered horizon and the fixed camera rig. With video recording enabled, the entry point writes scene_background.json beside the video directory. Save that manifest with the run. A successful run on one stage/background pair is a useful integration check; the complete scene track covers all 30 stages and three backgrounds. Inspect outcomes before aggregating Review a rollout video, verify the action dimension and image keys, and confirm that success is read from the environment's task predicate. Record episode success, steps, seed, task ID and any error separately. Failed environment initialization must not silently disappear from the planned evaluation matrix. Then follow the score protocol and save the reproduction artifacts . For model-specific action conversion, see Policy integration . ← Previous Training & baselines Next → Scene evaluation

title: Policy integration — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Policy integration Policy integration Build an adapter that preserves the environment's observation, action and stage-transition contract. Define the adapter boundary Your policy adapter translates the environment observation into model inputs and model predictions into controller targets. It should preserve the task's reset, success, termination and truncation behavior. Begin with one canonical stage and a short recorded rollout before attempting a full evaluation matrix. Read the registered robot, controller, action space and camera profile. Map images, proprioception, history and language into the model schema. Undo action normalization and convert predicted coordinates into the environment's joint order. Execute the chosen number of chunk actions at the 20 Hz control rate. At episode reset, clear policy history and cached action chunks. Convert coordinates explicitly Sharpa single-arm control has 29 absolute joint targets; bimanual control has 58. The bimanual order is left arm, right arm, left hand, right hand. These layouts describe Sharpa and do not specify the spaces of every supported embodiment. The GR00T reference adapter uses relative arm offsets internally and converts them back to absolute pd_joint_pos targets. Finger targets remain absolute. Passing offsets directly to the controller produces a different action even when the array has the expected width. Adapter component Check before evaluation Images Dataset camera → environment sensor mapping, color channels, resize/crop, normalization and history. State Field selection/order, task-dependent width, units and training-time statistics. Actions Joint order, radians, absolute/relative conversion, clipping and inverse normalization. Chunks Prediction horizon, executed actions per query and behavior when an episode ends mid-chunk. Language Canonical or registered instruction selection and any stage-specific instruction update. Compose stages without resetting the scene For a complete sequence, reset once at the beginning. Use the task's stage-success signals to update the instruction or select the next stage policy while preserving the simulator state. Resetting objects between stages changes the long-horizon task into separate skill evaluations. The paper's π0.5 composition switches stage-specific policies when a stage succeeds. GR00T uses a pooled task model with stage instructions. If your model keeps observation history or an action queue, define how those are handled when the stage changes and record that rule with the experiment. Use the reference path and record your changes Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. Inspect algo/groot.py , train/train_groot.py and train/train_configs/groot_config.py for the in-process GR00T path. ACT and Diffusion Policy expose their own image/state adapters and camera mappings in their training configurations. Keep the environment constructor separate from the model adapter so make_scene_eval_env can supply the fixed native-scene environment without changing the policy. Save the adapter revision, checkpoint hash, input schema and preprocessing configuration. Use Quick evaluation to validate the loop, then Scene evaluation to test transfer. ← Previous Embodiments Next → Data & replay

title: Data & replay — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Data & replay Data & replay Understand the paper's demonstrations, the recorded schema, and the difference between state restoration and action replay. What the paper reports The manuscript describes 3,000 replay-successful demonstrations : 100 for each of the 30 canonical stage tasks, recorded at 20 Hz, totaling approximately 9.1 hours. These are paper-reported dataset properties. A public download endpoint or dataset package has not been supplied. The collection pipeline records simulator state and actions, reviews pending episodes, exports accepted episodes and checks them in a fresh simulator. Offline rendering can produce multiple camera views from the recorded interaction. Data collection pipeline from the DexArena manuscript. Read the paper ↗ Inspect the recorded schema Feature Role observation.state Robot proprioception and task state; exact width and field layout depend on the task. action Absolute arm and hand joint targets in the collection controller's joint order. observation.environment_state Flattened simulator/environment state used for restoration and offline re-rendering. next.success The per-step task-success label computed during recording. episode.seed Reset seed used to reconstruct the episode context. Check the dataset's feature metadata, task/source fingerprint, controller and robot UID before loading it into a trainer. A simulator restoration state is not automatically an appropriate policy input: select the policy's state fields deliberately and preserve the choice in both training and online inference. Validate restoration and replay separately Review: inspect the pending episode and its video, including whether the task's physical success condition was reached. Restoration: load recorded frames into a fresh environment and compare the restored state and observations. Action replay: restore the recorded initial context, apply the recorded actions open-loop and test whether the task succeeds again. Export: retain the accepted episode's source metadata, seeds and validation results alongside the training data. Restoring rigid and articulated state does not restore the solver's transient contact cache. Contact-dependent quantities are excluded from frame-restoration equality checks; a visually similar restored frame does not prove the entire action trajectory will replay successfully. Run the research validators Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. These examples use a local dataset/session path. The tools inspect and replay existing recordings; prepare the matching runtime and preserve their JSON reports. python -m data_gen.replay.verify_recording_fidelity \ /path/to/lerobot-dataset \ --episodes 1 --stride 4 --action-replay \ --json-out fidelity.json python -m data_gen.replay.replay_success_rate \ /path/to/recording-session \ --jobs 2 --json-out replay-success.json Use data_gen/teleop/review_demos.py for review/export and data_gen/render/render_multiview_videos.py for offline rendering. Consult each tool's help and the dataset metadata before scaling up. Keep the raw recordings and validation reports so a later model conversion can be traced to its original data. Prepare data for a policy Split data by episode rather than by adjacent frames, record the training/validation episode lists, and fit normalization statistics only on the training split. Preserve camera mappings and any selected state dimensions. Continue with Training & baselines or the teleoperation workflow . ← Previous Policy integration Next → Teleoperation

title: Teleoperation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Teleoperation Teleoperation Prepare a matched control and mirror setup, collect a staged episode, and review it before training. From human motion to robot targets The paper's collection setup uses a Quest 3 headset, MANUS Meta Gloves Pro and controllers mounted on the backs of the hands. Wrist tracking drives arm inverse kinematics; calibrated finger retargeting produces hand-joint targets. The simulator supplies visual feedback and task-success signals. Choose a formal target from task/config/collection_targets.py . Match its task module, environment ID, robot UID and hand profile in the control and mirror processes. The canonical collection list has 10 complete tasks and 30 stages; legacy aliases are not additional collection targets. Prepare the operator and runtime Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. Verify the selected hand's SDK connection and the workstation's VR tracking before loading the task. Calibrate finger retargeting and verify left/right hand mapping, joint limits and wrist axes. Load the same environment and robot in the control and mirror processes, then confirm the shared workspace alignment. Use the launcher's --dry-run check to inspect environment, agent and joint wiring before collection. Test a short movement in simulation and confirm recording labels come from the environment's success predicate. The dry run constructs the configured environment and checks wiring; it still needs simulator assets and a renderer. It is not an SDK-free public installation test. Record to a pending store With the bridge, VR feedback and task profile configured, the mouse stage uses the following research recorder interface: python -m data_gen.teleop.manus_teleop \ --task office_mouse --env-id SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1 \ --robot-uids panda_sharpa_hand_right_angled_mobile_base \ --arm-ik nullspace --wrist-control --vr-project --vr-project-qpos \ --record --auto-segment --record-fps 20 --episode-seed 0 \ --record-pending-dir data/teleop_pending Add --dry-run to validate this launch without opening headset, glove or SDK connections. Actual collection also needs the calibrated operator profile and its matched mirror process. Use the task-specific launch profile for other targets. Review each pending episode and video before exporting it to the training dataset. Confirm the reset seed, task/source fingerprint and controller metadata, then run restoration and open-loop replay checks described in Data & replay . Check bridges and hand profiles The Sharpa bridge uses upstream port 2044 and downstream port 6668 . Wuji and XHand have their own SDK, retargeting and runtime profiles. Inspect the selected hand's configuration before reusing another hand's launch arguments. ss -ltnp '( sport = :2044 or sport = :6668 )' If a bridge reports an address-in-use error, identify the existing listener and reuse it or close its owning terminal cleanly. Match both ends when changing a connection. SDK credentials belong in the local runtime setup and should not enter dataset exports or shared logs. For policy-facing differences between hands, continue to Embodiments . ← Previous Data & replay Next → Training & baselines

title: Embodiments — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Embodiments Embodiments Understand supported end-effectors and the canonical Panda–Sharpa configuration used for the paper results. A shared task family, several interfaces DexArena's research code supports a parallel-jaw gripper and the Sharpa, Wuji and XHand dexterous hands. Each embodiment has its own robot description, controller layout and collection/retargeting configuration. The shared task family enables embodiment studies, but interface support alone does not establish comparable scores. End-effector Use and scope Parallel-jaw gripper Gripper-based task interfaces for cross-embodiment studies. Sharpa Hand 22 hand joints per side; Panda + Sharpa is the canonical setup for the manuscript's demonstrations and six-method evaluation. Wuji Hand A separate dexterous-hand robot and retargeting profile; read its registered spaces. XHand An additional hand interface with its own joint map, limits and runtime profile. Read the action space for the selected robot In the canonical Sharpa setup, one arm uses 7 arm joints plus 22 hand joints, for 29 absolute targets. Bimanual tasks concatenate left arm, right arm, left hand and right hand, for 58 targets. The control mode is pd_joint_pos . Do not reuse the Sharpa width or joint map for another hand. Inspect the registered robot UID, action space, joint names and limits, and verify the recorded dataset metadata. A matching array length does not establish a matching semantic joint order. Port a policy with an explicit mapping Confirm which stage environments are implemented for the desired robot and whether their success conditions and geometry match the comparison. Map the policy's proprioceptive fields to the robot's actual joints and sensors. Define the output conversion into absolute controller targets, including hand limits and any retargeting. Collect or validate embodiment-matched demonstrations rather than treating another hand's joint values as equivalent. Check short rollouts and replay before running a complete study. In the research checkout, inspect task/config/hand_variants.py and the relevant modules under task/robots/ . See Policy integration for the adapter contract. Report embodiment studies clearly State the robot/hand, task IDs, controller, action dimensions, camera profile and any task or asset changes. Publish embodiment-specific results separately from the canonical Panda–Sharpa manuscript scores. Avoid implying that every supported hand has a complete six-method benchmark table. Use Configurations to preserve the common workstation and timing, and the reproduction checklist to document the differences. ← Previous Configurations Next → Policy integration

title: Training & baselines — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Training & baselines Training & baselines Choose a baseline, preserve the data and control contract, and distinguish paper results from research entry points. Choose the learning setting Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. The manuscript evaluates six baselines: PPO, RLPD, ACT, Diffusion Policy, GR00T N1.7 and π0.5. They cover demonstration-guided reinforcement learning, imitation learning and vision-language-action adaptation. More algorithms exist in the research tree, but those entry points are not additional scored manuscript baselines. Before training, fix the canonical task, source revision, episode split, observation schema, cameras, instruction rule and absolute joint-target contract. Preserve the resolved trainer configuration and dataset identity with each checkpoint. Prepare data and configuration together Use utils/dex_tasks.py and task/config/collection_targets.py to resolve the task rather than inheriting a trainer's generic default environment. Match --env-id , --control-mode and the dataset/task configuration together. Some research defaults target unrelated ManiSkill tasks and are not DexArena presets. ACT and Diffusion Policy use preprocessed image datasets and camera/state mappings. GR00T needs its VLA dataset conversion, modality configuration and compatible base weights. Reinforcement-learning runs need the demonstration loader and reset-state assumptions to match the task. Check train/TRAIN_EVAL.md and the corresponding train/train_configs/ file before starting a run. python -m train.train_ACT --help python -m train.train_DP --help python -m train.train_ppo --help python -m train.train_rlpd --help python -m train.train_groot --help These help commands inspect the research entry points; they are not a complete installation or reproduction recipe. Model packages, datasets and assets must already be present. The six evaluated methods PPO The DexArena baseline augments PPO with behavior-cloning warm-up, behavior-cloning regularization, demonstration-state resets and demonstration-informed action statistics. Rewards are sparse task-success rewards. The reported PPO budget is one million environment steps per stage; the step-zero point of its training curves follows the cloning warm-up. Inspect train/train_ppo.py , train/train_configs/ppo_config.py and algo/ppo.py . Record the warm-up, reset distribution and training budget alongside the final checkpoint. Original paper ↗

title: Scene evaluation — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Scene evaluation Scene evaluation Evaluate a frozen policy across the three native kitchen scenes using one shared environment factory. The fixed three-scene matrix The default cross-scene track covers all 30 canonical stages on three named native kitchen backgrounds, for 90 task/background pairs. Freeze the learned policy and keep episode seeds and policy inputs consistent across the comparison. Background ID Native surface robocasa_l3_s2 Blue kitchen stone island robocasa_l3_s1 Light wood kitchen island robocasa_l3_s6 Warm wood kitchen stone island labutopia_lab003 is available for additional laboratory studies. It is optional and does not belong to the default three-kitchen matrix. Use the shared factory Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. from utils.dex_scene_eval import BACKGROUND_IDS, make_scene_eval_env env = make_scene_eval_env( "SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1", scene_background=BACKGROUND_IDS[0], obs_mode="rgb", # Use "state" for a state-based policy. ) try: obs, info = env.reset(seed=10001) background_manifest = env.unwrapped.eval_background_manifest # Continue with the frozen policy's observation/action adapter. # Save background_manifest with the episode results. finally: env.close() The factory accepts the 30 canonical subtasks. It enforces one CPU-physics environment, the registered robot and horizon, pd_joint_pos , reset-time reconfiguration and fixed 256 × 256 base/wrist policy cameras. Conflicting overrides raise an error. Understand what the scene changes The factory uses the native room's unscaled table and authored collision geometry. The original workspace table and ground have rendering and collisions disabled. At reset, the room is translated to align the robot-facing visible working edge with the original task table; the task's robot root, joint reset and object placements remain those of the task. A tabletop-height check rejects differences above 1 mm. This alignment does not make the tables physically identical: their dimensions and collision shapes can differ. Save eval_background_manifest , including its geometry and camera information, when reporting transfer results. Plan the matrix before running a policy python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --index 2 --out output/scene90/preview The preview saves policy-camera frames, diagnostic views and placement checks without loading a learned checkpoint. It requires the same project and scene assets plus a working renderer. A passed placement preview verifies scene construction, not policy success. Assign disjoint task/background/seed tuples to separate processes; see Parallel environments . Average stage success within each scene, then report mean and standard deviation across scene averages. See aggregation details . Optional procedural training variation is documented under Domain randomization . ← Previous Quick evaluation Next → Domain randomization

title: Domain randomization — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Domain randomization Domain randomization Use opt-in procedural variation for training or diagnostics while preserving a clear evaluation definition. Choose the variation for your experiment The reference scene-transfer track uses three fixed native kitchens. Procedural table textures, background surfaces and lighting are separate training or diagnostic options. State which variations the policy saw during training and keep the held-out evaluation scenes and checkpoint-selection rule explicit. The research RandomizedTableSceneBuilder has inert defaults: variation is enabled per axis. It supports appearance changes and optional table-height variation; it does not automatically update the placement of task-added objects. Enable appearance variation in a task Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. Inside the research task's scene-loading method, the builder can be configured as follows: from task.scene_builders import RandomizedTableSceneBuilder def _load_scene(self, options): self.table_scene = RandomizedTableSceneBuilder( env=self, random_table_texture=True, random_background=True, random_lighting=True, ) self.table_scene.build() Keep image observations enabled when studying visual robustness. Record the enabled axes, their parameter ranges, texture library and random seeds. Source references are task/scene_builders/ and docs/howto_randomize_scene.md in the research checkout. Handle height and camera changes deliberately If you enable random_table_height , use self.table_scene.table_top_offsets during episode initialization to shift every table-supported task actor consistently. The builder moves the table; it does not move bottles, tools or other task objects for you. Check contacts and success conditions after the geometry change. Cameras are owned by the task, not the scene builder. Any camera-pose jitter must be configured through the camera path and recorded separately. Keep evaluation at the defined fixed camera profile if you are reporting the native-scene track. Check that the experiment still measures its intended change Inspect several seeds and camera views, verify objects remain on their support surfaces, and check that task reset and success conditions still work. Compare appearance-only variation with geometry changes separately when interpreting outcomes. Report a custom randomization study with its own configuration and results. Use Scene evaluation for the standard three-kitchen protocol and Configurations for the fixed timing, controller and action contract. ← Previous Scene evaluation Next → Parallel environments

title: Parallel environments — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Parallel environments Parallel environments Scale the native-scene matrix through independent processes while retaining the registered evaluation contract. One native-scene environment per process make_scene_eval_env enforces num_envs=1 and sim_backend="physx_cpu" . The GR00T evaluation loop also requires num_eval_envs == 1 . These are properties of the inspected native-scene evaluation path. Run separate processes for disjoint tasks, backgrounds or episode-seed shards. General ManiSkill GPU-vectorized training capabilities do not establish vectorized support in this factory. For other training paths, inspect the algorithm's own environment and reset semantics before changing its environment count. Plan and shard scene previews Research checkout required The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces. python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \ --out output/scene90/preview --shard 0 --shards 3 --resume python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \ --out output/scene90/preview --shard 1 --shards 3 --resume python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \ --out output/scene90/preview --shard 2 --shards 3 --resume The three shard commands may run in separate terminals on a prepared machine. They are placement previews, not policy evaluation jobs. The preview tool isolates child asset caches; its resume logic checks passed records against source hashes and seeds. Retain failed logs for inspection. Partition policy work explicitly For policy sweeps, create a manifest with a unique tuple of task ID, background ID and episode seed for every planned episode. Assign each tuple to one worker, give workers distinct output directories, and pin the same checkpoint, adapter, task revision, camera profile and instruction rule. Keep renderer/device allocation explicit when several CPU-physics processes share a GPU for rendering or inference. Begin with a small number of workers and measure memory use before expanding. Process parallelism does not remove model or renderer resource requirements. Merge episodes before calculating scores Verify that all planned tuples are present exactly once. Keep runtime errors distinguishable from task failures and preserve enough logs to reproduce each one. A resumed run must not mix old and new checkpoints or task fingerprints. Calculate per-stage success from the merged episode records, then aggregate according to the score protocol . Averaging worker percentages can weight unequal shards incorrectly. Save the original plan, each worker's records and the final aggregation script as part of the reproduction package . ← Previous Domain randomization Next → Reproducibility & submission

title: Reproducibility & submission — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Reproducibility & submission Reproducibility & submission Prepare a reviewable experiment package while public leaderboard intake remains unavailable. Current submission status Preparation guide The leaderboard shows the six manuscript baselines. Public community intake, hosted policy execution and independent submission verification are not available yet. This page documents the evidence needed to make a local comparison reproducible; it is not an upload portal. First define which tracks you evaluated, freeze the policy and environment, and preserve the exact per-episode records from which your report is calculated. Build the reproduction package Artifact Include Source and runtime Repository/source revision, local changes, task fingerprint, adapter entry point, dependency versions and asset versions. Policy Method name, checkpoint identity/hash, compatible model configuration, training budget and preprocessing. Data Dataset identity/revision, episode split, filtering, camera/state selection and training-data scope. Environment Task IDs, robot UIDs, action order, controller, backend, horizon, camera profile and instruction rule. Episode manifest Every planned task/background/seed tuple, stage-transition rule and worker assignment where applicable. Outcomes Per-episode success, steps, stage trace, errors, logs, representative videos and the aggregation script. Use stable local filenames and include a short explanation of how the files relate. If you distribute your own model or data, include its access instructions and actual license; the code repository's license does not automatically determine the terms of every asset. Apply the declared evaluation units Stage execution uses 50 episodes for each of 30 stages in the training scene. Cross-scene evaluation uses 50 episodes per stage in each of the three native kitchens with a frozen policy. Long-horizon evaluation uses 50 episodes per sequence, with one reset at the beginning and no resets between stages. Weight stage tasks and complete sequences equally within their respective tracks. For cross-scene results, compute the stage average within each scene, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. Scene standard deviation describes variation across scenes, not a confidence interval over training seeds. Use matched episode seeds for a new method comparison and record the actual list. The paper's historical ACT/DP and GR00T runs use different recorded seed ranges; do not imply every manuscript method used identical seeds. Check a result before sharing it Verify that every planned episode appears once and that partial runs are labeled. Recalculate the summary from raw episode records and check task weighting. Inspect representative successes and failures, including a complete-sequence rollout. Confirm that the report identifies the canonical embodiment and any deviations from the protocol. Provide the DexArena citation and original method references. Use the score protocol for the reporting contract and Resources & release status for available public artifacts. ← Previous Parallel environments Next → Troubleshooting

title: Troubleshooting — DexArena Docs
text: Docs / Troubleshooting Troubleshooting Resolve source, asset, controller and replay mismatches before changing the benchmark configuration. Missing modules, registration or assets There is no task package after cloning the public repository The current official repository contains the README, Apache 2.0 license and repository metadata. The executable module examples require the asset-complete research source; there is no published DexArena package or asset download command to infer from these docs. Check release status . The environment ID is not registered Run from the prepared research checkout and import task before direct Gym creation. Check the exact ID in task/config/collection_targets.py ; aliases and retired curricula are not formal targets. A mesh or native kitchen cannot be loaded Verify project robot/object assets and the corresponding RoboCasa scene assets against the research revision. The paper, website images and preview videos are not installable simulator assets. Action and observation mismatches The action width is correct but the robot moves incorrectly Check semantic joint order, radians, inverse normalization and absolute/relative conversion. pd_joint_pos expects absolute targets. Sharpa has 29 targets for one arm and 58 for a dual-arm configuration; other hands have their own spaces. A model rejects state or image inputs Compare training and evaluation camera keys, resolutions, crops, channel ordering, temporal history and normalization. Task state widths vary. The native-scene factory's fixed camera rig can differ from ordinary task defaults. The scene factory rejects an override Use one CPU environment, the registered robot/horizon/controller and 256 × 256 policy cameras. Check the conflicting value against registered_task_settings ; do not bypass validation to force an incompatible run. Rendering and replay failures CPU physics still fails during rendering CPU physics and rendering are separate. The scene factory requires a render backend. Verify the local ManiSkill/SAPIEN renderer and graphics-driver setup, then try the smallest scene preview before loading a large model. A restored frame matches but the trajectory diverges Compare source fingerprints, reset seed, environment state, controller and background manifest. The solver's transient contact cache is not restored with rigid state. Use both frame-restoration validation and action replay rather than treating one as proof of the other. A sequence works only when reset between stages Check stage instructions, cached policy state and pending action chunks at transitions. The long-horizon protocol preserves simulator state after the initial reset; intermediate resets change the evaluation. Teleoperation bridge conflicts For the Sharpa bridge, inspect the configured ports before starting another process: ss -ltnp '( sport = :2044 or sport = :6668 )' Reuse the correct listener or close its owning terminal cleanly. If you change a bridge endpoint, update its paired endpoint as well. Wuji and XHand require their own profile checks. For any failed evaluation, retain the complete command, source revision, environment settings, seed, background manifest and error log. Reproduce it with the smallest relevant example from Quick evaluation or Scene evaluation before scaling back up. ← Previous Reproducibility & submission Next → Citation

title: Leaderboard protocol — DexArena
text: Leaderboard Score protocol Three evaluation tracks, explicit aggregation and a reproducible evidence trail. Manuscript baselines, not a verified community leaderboard The current scores are the six paper baselines. Public submission intake, remote execution and independent verification are not yet available. Evaluation units 01 Stage execution 30 stages × 50 episodes in the training scene. Each stage starts from its own valid reset distribution. 02 Cross-scene 30 stages × 3 native scenes × 50 episodes. Freeze the policy; retain the background manifest for every run. 03 Long-horizon 10 sequences × 50 episodes. Reset once per episode, never between stages; measure final sequence completion. How scores are aggregated Stage and long-horizon averages weight tasks equally. For cross-scene results, average stage success within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. The ± value is scene variation, not a training-seed confidence interval. The original manuscript records ACT/DP stage seeds 50000–50049 and GR00T seeds 10001–10050. New comparison sweeps should use matched episode seeds across methods and record the manifest; do not imply the paper used identical seed ranges for every method. Keep task horizons and physical success predicates fixed. Persistent hold counters or latches are part of the task definition. π0.5 switches stage models for composition; GR00T uses a pooled task model with stage instructions. Reproduction package Identity Environment/task revision, robot UID, controller, horizon and seeds. Policy Checkpoint hash, adapter revision, training-data scope and observation preprocessing. Scenes Background IDs, camera profile and source/geometry manifests. Outcomes Per-episode success, steps, stage trace, logs, videos and aggregation script.
